two main questions: (i) Can we learn a mixture of univariate Gaussians in the private setting, and if so, how many samples are sufficient? (ii) Can we learn mixtures of axis-aligned Gaussians, and if so how many samples are necessary?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for mixtures of $k$ Gaussians, we achieve a sample complexity of $\widetilde O(kd)$, matching the sample complexity for the non-private setting.
we provide the first differentially private algorithms for learning unbounded mixtures of multivariate Gaussians with arbitrary covariance matrices.
we provide a complete characterization for privately learning mixures of axis-aligned Gaussians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of privately learning Gaussian mixtures can be solved efficiently, even when the covariance matrix has full rank.
, for learning mixtures, it is possible to achieve the best known sample complexity without sacrificing too much in terms of privacy.
